svg.title: Related medial-pallial territories in differently built tetrapod brains
svg.desc: A branching tree of four sampled living lineages (frog Xenopus laevis; mouse; turtle Trachemys scripta; chicken) sits above one simplified, source-based transverse hemisection of the telencephalon for each species, all oriented dorsal up and medial left and not to scale. A shared muted teal marks the illustrated medial-pallial territories and derivatives: the medial and dorsomedial pallium of the adult frog, the hippocampal formation of the mouse at embryonic day 18.5, the medial and dorsomedial cortex of the adult turtle, and the dorsomedial hippocampal formation of the chicken at embryonic day 16. White spaces are ventricles. In the chicken, the teal band continues laterally beyond the bracketed hippocampal formation into further medial-pallial derivatives. A separate enlarged inset of the chicken hippocampal region uses dashed outlines and hatching to show a finer, proposed correspondence: much of the V-shaped area as dentate-gyrus-like and its dorsal tip as CA3-like.

g.text: Branch lengths do not represent time
The shared color marks a regional relationship. It does not imply
identical adult architecture or a one-to-one match between subdivisions.
Sections not to scale. Stages differ (adult or late embryo) and are not developmentally equivalent.
Simplified from published schematic sections; frog and turtle drawings mirrored to share one orientation.
All sections: dorsal up, medial left
